It computes the sources explicitly: N lines U_a. For the sinks it computes 'Nm+N(m-1)+(W-2N)m=Wm-N' from the terminal table.
'A wire enters and leaves each gate with that gate's label, so its signed changes telescope to sink minus source dimension, summing to Wm-2N'. This is the paper's telescoping at gates.

It sets up A, P, B, Q and the [G|E] notation, splits A' into four orthogonal pieces to get B'=P'^⊥=(B⊗F)⊥(P⊗t^⊥), and matches the outgoing labels to the next stage's incoming ones. It checks both ends: U_a and 0 at stage 1; F and U_a^⊥ at stage 3 because P'=U_a.

The definition is given in full: 'a vertex labelled U gets the projection Π_U onto U along U^⊥, except sources: -Π_{U_a} at X_a, else 0=Π_0'.
'The negative source makes every route's endpoint difference Id, the same shear on every role'. The page checks this route by route.

The number 177176569088785861287000000 appears only in a quoted citation and is not computed on the page. The value is correct: W_bm-N+2L_b with L_b=784406700000000.

From F=U⊥(U'∩U^⊥)⊥U'^⊥, 'Both projections fix U and vanish on U'^⊥, but only Π_{U'} fixes U'∩U^⊥, so Π_{U'}-Π_U projects onto U'∩U^⊥ and has rank dim U'-dim U, as does its negative on a reversed edge'. This is the paper's argument made explicit.
'each edge's rank is its absolute dimension change, except the first edge of each X_a'. This holds because every other vertex matrix is Π of its label, including 0=Π_0 at the other sources.
'at stage 1, B=0, so it joins U_a to [F|⟨t_{a_1}⟩]=U_a with zero change, yet its matrix Π_{U_a}-(-Π_{U_a})=2Π_{U_a} has image the line U_a and rank one'.
'The deficit W_bm-s_b=N-2L_b=339/539 N is positive as L_b/N<1/2'. This matches the paper and the arithmetic is correct.
'Π_{U_a^⊥}+Π_{U_a} from X_a to Y_a, Π_F-0 elsewhere'. This equals Id because F=U_a⊥U_a^⊥ (stated earlier on the page) and matches the paper's P_{U_a^⊥}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m.
